o.text: From Persian کند (kand), ultimately from Sanskrit खण्ड (khaṇḍa, “candied sugar”), root खण्ड् (khaṇḍ, “to divide, break into pieces”), or from Proto-Dravidian *kaṇṭu; compare Tamil கண்டு (kaṇṭu, “hard candy”).
From Arabic لَا (lā, “no”) + قَيْد (qayd, “effort”). Compare Turkish lakayt.
Borrowed from Persian زاغچه (zâġče), the diminutive form of زاغ (zâġ).
